The Anglican Diocese of Lagos West has celebrated the 90th birthday of its Lord Chancellor, Justice Babasola Ogunade (retd.), with a special thanksgiving service and the launch of his autobiography titled God’s Hand in My Life. The celebration, which attracted eminent bishops of the Anglican Communion, clergy, church officials, family members and well-wishers, was held on Monday, November 16, 2026, at Christ Anglican Church in the Agege area of the state. The thanksgiving service was presided over by the Bishop of the Diocese of Lagos West, the Rt Rev Dr James Odedeji, who described the nonagenarian as a man of exceptional integrity, diligence and honesty, according to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Tuesday. Delivering the sermon, the Bishop of Ibadan North Diocese and Archbishop of the Ibadan Province, Church of Nigeria, the Most Reverend Dr Williams Aladekugbe, who represented the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, said the celebrant’s contributions to the Anglican Communion extended far beyond the Diocese of Lagos West. He recalled the celebrant’s decade-long service as head of the House of Laity of the Church of Nigeria between 2010 and 2020, describing him as a shining light within the church and a worthy role model for younger generations, the report said in part. Speaking at the launch, renowned chemical engineering scholar, Prof. Ogunye, described Ogunade as a “community leader and tireless advocate for truth and justice”. He particularly commended Justice Ogunade’s efforts in providing free legal advice and support to vulnerable members of society over the years. Reviewing the book, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Barrister Adebambo Adesanya, who serves as Registrar of the Diocese of Lagos West, praised the former judge’s determination and resilience in pursuing his ambitions despite numerous challenges. He recounted one of the inspiring stories captured in the autobiography, detailing how Justice Ogunade secured admission for studies abroad but lacked the financial resources to proceed. According to Adesanya, the young Ogunade sought help from an aunt who had just received proceeds from a thrift contribution. Moved by his determination, she gave him the entire sum and assisted in raising additional funds to support his education. The experience, he noted, became a defining moment in Justice Ogunade’s life, shaping his values of selflessness, sacrifice and commitment to empowering younger people, the statement read. Dignitaries at the event included the Chief Judge of Ogun State, Justice Mosunmola Dipeolu; the President of Ogun State Customary Court of Appeal, Justice Adebisi Femi-Segun; and the Pro-Chancellor of Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo, Dr Olutoyin Okeowo, among others. Born on November 16, 1936, in Ijebu-Igbo, Ogun State, Ogunade obtained his law degree in 1970 and built a distinguished career at both the Bar and the Bench. He later served as a High Court Judge in Ogun State until his retirement. In 1999, he was appointed the pioneer Chancellor of the Anglican Diocese of Lagos West, a position he continues to hold more than two decades later.
